events.title: Traditional Birth of Siddhartha Gautama (Buddha)
events.description: In many East Asian Buddhist traditions, April 8 is celebrated as the birthday of Siddhartha Gautama, the founder of Buddhism, traditionally said to have been born in Lumbini, in present-day Nepal. The date is observed as Hanamatsuri in Japan and Buddha's Birthday in Korea and elsewhere. The year is a traditional estimate and is disputed by scholars.
events.significance: The observance marks the birth of the figure whose teachings gave rise to Buddhism, one of the world's major religions, and it remains a major annual festival across East Asia.

events.title: Venus de Milo Discovered
events.description: A peasant named Yorgos Kentrotas found the ancient Greek statue Venus de Milo on the island of Milos. The marble sculpture, thought to date from roughly 150-125 BCE, was acquired by France and presented to Louis XVIII, who donated it to the Louvre.
events.significance: The statue became one of the most famous works of ancient Greek sculpture and a major attraction at the Louvre Museum in Paris.

events.title: Superconductivity Discovered by Heike Kamerlingh Onnes
events.description: Dutch physicist Heike Kamerlingh Onnes observed that the electrical resistance of mercury dropped to zero when cooled to near absolute zero (about 4 kelvin) in his laboratory at Leiden.
events.significance: The discovery of superconductivity opened a major field of physics and led to technologies such as MRI machines, particle accelerators, and maglev trains.

events.title: Death of Pablo Picasso
events.description: Pablo Picasso, the Spanish painter and sculptor, died at age 91 at his home in Mougins, France. He had co-founded Cubism and produced works such as Les Demoiselles d'Avignon and Guernica over a career lasting more than seven decades.
events.significance: Picasso was one of the most influential artists of the 20th century, and his death marked the end of an era in modern art.

events.title: Death of Margaret Thatcher
events.description: Margaret Thatcher, the first female Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, died at age 87 after suffering a stroke. She served from 1979 to 1990 and was known for her free-market economic policies, her confrontations with trade unions, and the Falklands War.
events.significance: Thatcher was one of the most influential and polarizing political leaders in modern British history, and her policies reshaped the UK economy and politics.
